title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT, success target 0.39

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (design of public submission 3da91365-2d58-40e5-ac7d-415e3061f7d8: compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, partition and distinguished bits taken from the raw class key, deterministic class-consistent fruitless-cycle escape, a 40/theta stuck-walk restart, and a distinguished-report log of hard capacity C_rep = 2^66 records (direct addressing, 80 bytes each) with an abort-on-overflow failure rule whose probability is Chernoff-bounded below 2^-1000, matched offline by an in-place heapsort with at most 67 sift levels per record and a cap of 2^40 confirmations; output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.861 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling charged at its worst case (2^64.64 units at the cap), cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. Peak memory is below 2^72.33 bytes (a hard bound: the 2^66-record log at 80 bytes per record plus the multiplier table and walk states, with no hash table); preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for R-adding rho walks (with the Brent-Pollard R/(R-1) correction and 3% explicit step slack; model success 0.4081 at the step budget), the same heuristic also giving the fruitless-cycle rates derived in proof.md section 3.2 and the Chernoff bound on the report count; it is supported by toy-field experiments that run the production partition and distinguished-point predicates; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements, check the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula, distinctness of the 12 keys, consistency of the canonical representative, p^6 = inversion, ord_r(p)=12. Part B: run the complete Frobenius-class rho walk (kappa trick, twisted table, partition h = K mod R and distinguished test on the raw class key as in production, 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes, stuck-walk rule, collision solving) in a field q near 2^20 with the same tower shape and report collision times against the 0.39 budget S0 and 1.03 S0, cycle rates and the distinguished fraction. Part A2: measure the low 70 bits of the class key on real GT elements. Part C: recompute the fruitless-cycle bound, the report-cap Chernoff exponent, the memory bound, the worst-case report-handling charge and the work ledger. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs.
